name: Ruth Eade
life: Ruth grew up in a house staged for sale every spring. She knows how exhausted a family can become trying to look as if it has never used its own kitchen. She has started scheduling viewings around one untouched family meal. Tuesday often includes a stop at Breakwater Way, where Ruth stops on the landward side of the cycle track to watch the first boats turn for home.
voice: I described it as original hardware. When the owner started to cry I crossed the phrase out. I still need the commission to cover my own rent, and I'll earn it with a different sentence.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a cream pullover and a partly rubbed-away embroidered initial. Ruth has a strong profile and a little space between the front teeth, with a cropped cut that shows the shape of the ears. Ruth counts on the side of one finger where hardly anybody notices during a conversation.
personality: Ruth can be wonderfully decisive about an emergency and maddeningly undecided about a gift. This is because a person can say precisely what hurts and rarely says exactly what they want.
agenda: To sell the house with terms the owner can sign freely.
family: Ariel Powell is Ruth’s parent’s cousin. Ruth checks the date twice. Ariel brings something that can still be enjoyed tomorrow. Arrangements do change in their family. Taking a delay seriously without treating it as an insult took both of them years. Asked about *The last home visit*, Ariel says, “I brought sweet tea for years. My oldest client said she'd waited for my last day to admit she liked it bitter.”
connections: Verity Long. The prospective buyer and agent must decide what a lodger means for the old owner's conditions.

reactions.situation: A shift worker turns up after the porch goes dark
reactions.response: Ruth keeps the worker company at the gate and lets the homeowner explain the dark.

reactions.situation: Someone begins blaming the youngest worker for a missing item
reactions.response: Ruth brings the worker into the conversation and asks what they remember without feeding them a story.

reactions.situation: If a neighbor offers a costly present
reactions.response: Ruth asks for an afternoon to work out whether accepting it would put someone else in debt.
